results.summary: This design implements a spiking neural network with 18 programmable digital LIF neurons and 144 synapses arranged in three fully connected layers. It is configured via an SPI interface to set neuron thresholds, decay rates, refractory periods, and synaptic weights and delays. Input spikes are applied to the first layer, and output spikes or membrane potentials can be read back through SPI. The project is notable for being generated by ChatGPT and for its use of programmable delays, though no silicon test results are provided.

This is a Verilog implementation of the classic Space Invaders game. The player controls a ship using three input buttons to move left, move right, and shoot, with the game state output on eight pins. It is intended to be played using the TinyTapeout Commander app, which maps keyboard inputs to the ASIC pins, and tested with the TinyTapeout VGA Playground. No external hardware is required beyond the standard TinyTapeout setup, and no silicon test results are mentioned.

This project is a scaled-down version of the Spacewar game with VGA output, based on the VGA playground controller example. It accepts a SNES gamepad for input and outputs VGA signals, and also supports an audio PMOD. The design was left incomplete due to the Efabless shutdown, so it only allows moving a square on the screen rather than being a full game. It is configured for the demoscene competition and requires external VGA and gamepad hardware.

This design is an SPI-controlled PWM generator with eight bidirectional IO pins. It contains eight registers accessible via two different SPI interfaces (clocked and sampled) to configure PWM on-time and cycle, as well as IO direction and values. The design includes test modes for SPI reads/writes, PWM output, external PWM control, and bidirectional IO. It requires an external SPI master for configuration and testing.

This design implements a stochastic integrator using Euler's method in the stochastic computing domain. It takes two serial inputs and produces multiple serial outputs representing different integrator configurations. The design is based on published research and uses LFSRs for stochastic number generation. Testing involves setting the inputs to constant high and low to observe the integration behavior, and external hardware such as an ADALM2000 may be used for signal generation and analysis.

This project is a simple 8-bit CPU architecture implemented in SystemVerilog. It interfaces with external QSPI flash and RAM memories through dedicated chip select and data pins. The design is intended to be a minimal CPU, but the documentation is very sparse, providing only the title and pin names without detailed operation or testing instructions. No silicon test results are available.

This is a factory test module for Tiny Tapeout subtiles, designed to verify all available I/O. It has three modes controlled by reset and clock signals: mirroring inputs to outputs, inverting inputs to outputs, or driving outputs low. The design is implemented in a single line of Verilog and is used to test the connectivity of subtile pins on an ASIC. It is a simple utility with no external hardware requirements.

This design is an 8-channel customizable beamforming signal processor for audio applications. It accepts PDM microphone inputs and outputs PCM audio, with delay selection via pins. The documentation is extremely thin, consisting of placeholder text, so the exact functionality and testing procedure are unclear. External hardware includes PDM microphones, a clock generator, and an I2S receiver.

This project displays a running sushi animation on a VGA screen. It outputs VGA signals and requires a TinyVGA PMOD for connection. The design is a simple demo with minimal documentation, and no silicon test results are provided. It is intended for visual demonstration.

This is a simple monophonic synthesizer with PWM audio output. It uses five input pins for note enable signals and eight switches to select sounds or notes, producing left and right PWM outputs. External hardware includes five IR modules to generate notes, eight switches, and two low-pass filters to produce audio signals. The design is a basic synth with limited documentation.
